title: Session Structure
subtitle: Prepare, train, monitor, debrief and document
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating session structure within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain session structure without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in session structure.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to session structure.

sections.explainSimply: A session usually includes symptom check, electrode setup, baseline, training blocks, breaks and review.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Block length and total dose should reflect tolerance, age, target and adverse-response monitoring. Functional outcomes matter more than game scores.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Document state, medications, sleep, food, caffeine, protocol parameters, reward rate, artifacts, subjective response and planned adjustments.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A rehabilitation plan: define the target, dose, measurement and stopping rule before changing the exercise.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand session structure to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Longer sessions can amplify fatigue and adverse effects rather than accelerate learning.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using session structure predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: Longer sessions can amplify fatigue and adverse effects rather than accelerate learning. Evidence classification: practitioner consensus.

quizBank.question: What is the central clinical point of Session Structure?
options: A session usually includes symptom check, electrode setup, baseline, training blocks, breaks and review.
Protocol choice requires no outcome measurement
Artifact is irrelevant once feedback begins
quizBank.explanation: A session usually includes symptom check, electrode setup, baseline, training blocks, breaks and review.

quizBank.question: Which limitation matters most when interpreting Session Structure?
options: Longer sessions can amplify fatigue and adverse effects rather than accelerate learning.
quizBank.explanation: Longer sessions can amplify fatigue and adverse effects rather than accelerate learning.

quizBank.question: How should the evidence for Session Structure be communicated?
options: As practitioner consensus, with methods and outcomes specified
As conclusively effective for all clients
By promising normalisation of the brain
quizBank.explanation: The appropriate evidence label is: practitioner consensus.
